# Grid cells keep stale content when a replacement record keeps its key

## Context

A browser probe during neomjs/neo-agent-institution#671 found that `useInternalId: false` left a thread button showing its old expanded state after fresh mailbox records were assigned. That consumer retained internal IDs and selection rebinding; the Engine defect remains separate.

A fresh single-thread Grid/Store probe reproduces it: replace `{id: 'same', name: 'before'}` with `{id: 'same', name: 'after'}` through `Store.setData(..., {continuation: true})`. The row holds the fresh record with name `after`, but its plain cell and Button still show `before`; the pooled Button still references the old record. The relevant Row/Body/Component files match dev `a852b8ca6e`.

## The Problem

The store key is stable across snapshots, while each snapshot contains fresh record instances. Cell reuse mistakes the unchanged key for unchanged data. This affects plain cells as well as component cells and can leave actions bound to a retired record.

## The Architectural Reality

`Body.getRecordId()` uses the store key in semantic-key mode. `Row.updateContent()` notices a changed record instance, assigns it, then forwards `recycle: true` to `createVdom()`. Both pooled and permanent cell fast paths compare only `oldNode.data.recordId`, so neither calls the renderer. `Component.cellRenderer()` already distinguishes instance/version and can rebind the existing component correctly when reached.

Design authority: `Row.updateContent` promises to "trigger a VDOM update to reflect the new data"; `Component.useBindings` documents that record-specific component config "is updated on every recycle". The observed stale output contradicts these owning contracts.

## The Fix

In `Row.updateContent`, allow cell-VDOM reuse only when the record instance is retained. Keep component pooling and the existing render paths. Extend existing Store/grid coverage with changed-value snapshots sharing a key, repeated replacement, continuation, and same-instance reuse controls. No new module or abstraction is needed.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Row.updateContent({record, recycle})` | `src/grid/Row.mjs`, `updateContent` | A fresh record invokes cell rendering even when its key matches; same-instance recycling remains available | Explicit `recycle: false` prevents cell reuse when rendering runs | Owning JSDoc | Replacement and reuse regression controls |
| `Component.cellRenderer` | `src/grid/column/Component.mjs` | Existing component is rebound to the fresh record, without replacement of the component | Existing renderer behavior | Owning JSDoc unchanged | Instance identity, record binding, and rendered text assertions |

Decision Record impact: none — restores existing grid rendering contracts. Agent OS structure-map: N/A (Body-only repair).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Red-first coverage observes stale rendered content for a fresh record with the same semantic key, across pooled plain and permanent component cells.
- [ ] Ordinary replacement and continuation, including a second replacement back to the original value, render current data and bind the retained component to the fresh record.
- [ ] Same-instance forced recycling retains its cell node and avoids redundant renderer calls; hide/rebind remains correct.
- [ ] Relevant grid units and browser coverage pass; no added structural row churn or component replacement.

## Out of Scope

FM's selection/key-mode policy, same-instance row-index-dependent renderers, the separate keyboard-selection investigation in `#19515`, and new Store semantics.

## Avoided Traps

No unconditional rerender on every scroll, no component destruction/recreation, and no retained record object in VDOM metadata. `#17401` was a component update-depth issue; `#18186` was dropped in favor of the config-sharing fix `#18192`, not a decision against fresh-record rendering.
